description.text: Girolamo Recanati Capodiferro was born in Rome on 22 June 1502 to the patrician families of Recanati and Capodiferro. From a young age he entered the service of Cardinal Alessandro Farnese, the future Pope Paul III, and later received a series of appointments in the Roman Curia under Pope Clement VII, including several diplomatic missions.

In 1541 he was named nuncio to Portugal and then to France, where he announced the calling of the Council of Trent. He became a cardinal deacon in December 1544, was appointed papal legate in Romagna, and played a key role in the conclaves that elected Popes Julius III, Marcellus II, Paul IV, and Pius IV. He died on 1 December 1559 during the conclave that elected Pius IV and was buried in Santa Maria della Pace.

curiosities.text: He was the cardinal who announced the measures the Papal States would take to defend itself against a possible Ottoman attack.
He served as datary from 1541 to 1544 and as treasurer of the Apostolic Camera in 1541.
He proposed a marriage between a French princess and the pope's natural son to Francis I of France.
